clusters.name: Your grandfather Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's collapse and death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to her mother Odette's every evening; your father Duncan took night shifts and distanced from Odette; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and was warned at work; he and Celeste separated; Odette lay awake over them; and your brother Callum had ear infections through the winter. Your father's anxiety and uncle's symptom are not directly told but emerge from the pile of shifts around the death and its aftermath.

clusters.name: Your mother Odette's bed rest in pregnancy, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother Odette ordered to bed in March 1984: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house; your father Duncan argued with his mother over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it; and you could not sleep without your father by the bed. These shifts lie within four months and centre on the household's strain as your grandmother overfunctioned and your father's anxiety rose around the pregnancy.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: From your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986 to your grandfather Ambrose giving up his workshop in February 1996: your grandfather took over her cooking and appointments; your father Duncan phoned his father every night for news; Hazel had a bad fall and walked with a frame; your father and uncle Lyle argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather's chest pains began; your father drank most evenings; Hazel could no longer dress or stand and needed a nurse; and your father fought with your mother Odette over his evenings at his parents' house. The shifts build slowly over a decade as her decline deepened and the family's effort to manage it grew, with your father's drinking and your grandfather's decline marking the strain.

clusters.name: Your brother Callum's move north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for a job up north in May 1999: your father Duncan argued with him over his plans; your mother Odette could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school through the autumn; your mother took Ines everywhere, even to work; and by August 2000 Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams. The shifts show your mother's anxiety and your sister's decline, with your mother turning toward your sister as Callum moved away.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003: you could not sleep more than a few hours and stopped going to the bookshop by April, losing the job in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark by August; you stopped returning your mother's calls; and by November you took a job at the garden centre and slept through the night again. Every shift in these months is yours alone, and no one else's shows.
